title_as_printed: Similar Theory of Mind Deficits in Community Dwelling Older Adults with Vascular Risk Profile and Patients with Mild Cognitive Impairment: The Case of Paradoxical Sarcasm Comprehension

blind_codes.Sample_N: 109 (41 VRF + 44 MCI + 24 HC; Table 1 lists HC n = 22)

blind_code_notes: Category: C4 arguable (behavioural measure of language/sarcasm comprehension).

registry_codes.Sample_N_Approx: 109 — 41 VRF / 44 MCI / 24 HC (text; Table 1 lists HC n=22)

Task_Type.reason: MANOVA/ANOVA group-mean comparisons of TASIT scores across VRF, MCI and healthy controls; no discrimination figure.
Task_Type.quote: The analyses carried out were MANOVA and ANOVA. The main aim of the analysis was to compare the performance of the three groups.

Category.reason: Two honest readings. The sole data are scores on a standardised neuropsychological social-cognition test (TASIT Part 2) given within a neuropsychological battery, which fits C5 (neuropsych). The test measures comprehension of sarcasm from dialogue and paralinguistic cues, a behavioural language measure, which gives C4 some basis.
Category.quote: all participants were evaluated with an extensive neuropsychological battery and selected for the purpose of the study, which thoroughly assesses memory capacity, complex executive functioning ability, emotion recognition and social cognition [p.7] / examining a person’s ability to perceive social inference, specifically inferences involved in the use of sarcasm within a minimal context. [p.6]

Validation_Type.reason: Group comparison; no predictive model validated.

Sample_N_Approx.reason: 109 in text and abstract (41 + 44 + 24); the registry correctly notes the Table 1 HC count of 22.
Sample_N_Approx.quote: The sample comprised 109 adults with Greek origin (24 males, 85 females).

ADNI_Dependent.reason: Greek clinic and community samples; no ADNI data.

notes: No field in error. Category C4 vs C5 shifts one study between the behavioural/digital and clinical/neuropsych domain tallies; C5 is the more literal reading.
